title.narrative: DRRS South Sudan 2024 – Follow-up IOM Bentiu

description.narrative: South Sudan has been heavily impacted by climate induced floods over the last years. Since 2019, over a million people have lost businesses, farms, animals, belongings and homes and had to seek safety in other places, away from their homes. Most of the affected areas largely fall within the Sudd Valley along the White Nile, like Bentiu, Bor, Ayod, Fangak, Pibor, and Malakal. These floods have severely affected the ability of the South Sudanese to recover from the effects of years of civil conflict and build resilience, and it has been exacerbating the already dire humanitarian situation in the country.In early 2021 the International Organization of Migration (IOM) reached out to the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) with a request for technical assistance on flood risk mitigation and management in South Sudan. This request was granted and resulted in a historical climate assessment and a hydrological and hydraulics model for Bentiu and its surrounding areas. Over the course of 2023, IOM managed to further develop this model with the aim to support not only for the flood preparation and response but also long-term programming. Based on the combined assessments, it has become apparent that the floods of the last years seem to have been caused by very intense rainfall in the North and South upstream areas in Bentiu. This intensification of rainfall patterns is a climate change induced trend in the region, despite declining average annual rainfall. As such, these flooding patterns are expected to be repeated in 2024 with dire consequences. In this light, the objective of this assignment is to follow up on the work undertaken to support IOM South Sudan on flood preparation and response; to identify any gaps in terms of urgent support needed, and if applicable, to advise on which organisation or actor could possibly play a role in picking this up.
